mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which may lead to decreased borrowing and investment, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX shows positive returns despite high FEDFUNDS, hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in unemployment rate below 4% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and increasing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 4%, hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and low unemployment indicate strong economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 rises and UNRATE is low but SPX returns are negative, hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, high FEDFUNDS may signal monetary tightening, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If high FEDFUNDS in late-cycle doesn't lead to negative SPX returns, hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment indicates a strong job market, boosting S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but SPX returns are negative, hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production above 100 indicates strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO exceeds 100 but SPX returns are negative, hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPI) and high FEDFUNDS may indicate stagflation, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPI and FEDFUNDS are high but SPX returns are positive, hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real savings indicate increased consumer spending, boosting S&P 500 returns in an early expansion.
failure_condition: If RSAFS rises in early-cycle but SPX returns are negative, hypothesis fails.
